description: Two-step 3D reconstruction workflow: Ab Initio Reconstruction → Homogeneous Refinement

steps.1: Ab Initio Reconstruction (homo_abinit) - Generate initial 3D model

description.type: STEP 1: Ab initio reconstruction to generate initial 3D model

description.num_classes: Number of 3D classes to generate (1 for homogeneous dataset)
description.initial_resolution: Starting resolution in Angstroms for ab initio
description.final_resolution: Target resolution in Angstroms for ab initio (don't set < 8 Å initially)
description.max_iterations: Maximum number of iterations for ab initio (50 is typical)
description.symmetry: Symmetry group - C1 (no symmetry), C2-C9 (cyclic), D2-D9 (dihedral), T, O, I

description.type: STEP 2: Homogeneous refinement to improve resolution
description.resolution: Target resolution for refinement in Angstroms (optional, null for auto)

homogeneous_single_class.description: Single homogeneous structure using ab initio - most common case

homogeneous_reconstruction_fast.description: Single homogeneous structure using homogeneous reconstruction - faster alternative

high_resolution.description: High resolution refinement after ab initio

reconstruction_method.ab_initio: Standard method, supports multiple classes (1-4), works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous datasets
reconstruction_method.homogeneous: Faster alternative optimized for single structure, often more robust for homogeneous datasets
reconstruction_method.recommendation: Try homogeneous reconstruction first for known homogeneous datasets; use ab initio when heterogeneity is suspected

num_classes.1: Use when all particles represent the same structure (homogeneous dataset)
num_classes.2-3: Use when mild structural heterogeneity is expected
num_classes.3-4: Use when significant structural variation is present
num_classes.note: More classes = longer computation time (only applies to ab initio)

resolution.initial_resolution: Start at 20-30 Å for stable convergence
resolution.final_resolution: Set to 8-12 Å for ab initio (don't go lower than 8 Å)
resolution.refinement_resolution: Can target higher resolution (3-5 Å) during refinement
resolution.note: Better resolution comes from refinement, not initial ab initio

symmetry.CN: Cyclic symmetry (C2, C3, C5, etc.) - use if known
symmetry.DN: Dihedral symmetry (D2, D7, etc.) - use if known
symmetry.warning: Wrong symmetry can cause artifacts - only use if certain!

iterations.50: Standard number of iterations for most cases
iterations.100: Use for difficult cases with poor initial models
iterations.note: Monitor convergence in CryoSPARC - job may finish earlier if converged

refinement_type.none: No refinement - just generate initial model with ab initio
refinement_type.homogeneous: Use when ab initio shows one good class - refines single structure
refinement_type.heterogeneous: Use when ab initio shows multiple distinct structures - refines all simultaneously

quick_validation.description: Quick reconstruction to check if particles are good
steps: Run homogeneous reconstruction (faster) OR ab initio with num_classes=1
Run ab initio with num_classes=1 OR homogeneous reconstruction
Optionally run homogeneous refinement for better resolution
Run homogeneous reconstruction (often faster than ab initio)
Optionally run homogeneous refinement for better resolution
Run heterogeneous refinement with selected classes
Run ab initio with appropriate symmetry
Run homogeneous refinement with same symmetry for high resolution

reconstruction_methods: Choose ab initio for heterogeneous datasets or when multiple classes are expected
Choose homogeneous reconstruction for faster results with homogeneous datasets
Homogeneous reconstruction is often more robust and faster for single structure cases
Both methods work without requiring a reference model
ab_initio: Ab initio is computationally intensive and can take hours
No reference model needed - generates structures de novo
Works best with at least 10,000-50,000 particles
Multiple classes help identify heterogeneity but increase runtime
Initial model quality improves with more particles and better SNR
homogeneous_reconstruction: Often faster than ab initio for homogeneous datasets
Uses a different algorithm optimized for single structure reconstruction
Good alternative when ab initio struggles to converge
Can achieve better initial resolution (8 Å vs 10-12 Å for ab initio)
Particularly effective with high-quality, well-aligned particles
refinement: Refinement is optional but recommended for high-resolution structures
Homogeneous refinement is faster and works for single structures
Heterogeneous refinement simultaneously classifies and refines
Can significantly improve resolution beyond ab initio
Best results come from iterative cycles of refinement
best_practices: For homogeneous datasets, try homogeneous reconstruction first (often faster)
For heterogeneous datasets or when uncertain, use ab initio
Check reconstruction results in CryoSPARC before refinement
Use conservative resolution targets for initial reconstruction
Save aggressive resolution targeting for refinement stages
Monitor FSC curves to track resolution improvement
If one method fails, try the alternative (ab initio vs homogeneous reconstruction)
